# SuperSplit

> A free bill splitting web app that runs entirely in the browser. Split group
> expenses including taxes and fees, uneven payers, percentage and share
> splits and bill round-off, then settle up and share a receipt. It works
> fully offline, needs no account, and stores everything on the device.

SuperSplit is at https://lowkey.tools/supersplit/ and is open source at
https://github.com/shrinathprabhu/supersplit. It is built by Shrinath Prabhu
(https://shrinath.me), from the makers of OwlEye Analytics
(https://owleye.dev). Free, no accounts, no adverts, no tracking, no server.

## What it does

- **Groups.** One group per trip, flat or dinner. Add people by name; each
  gets a generated avatar. Mark one person as yourself and every screen shows
  your own position.
- **Expenses.** Enter the amount before tax, then attach any number of taxes
  and fees, each a percentage (GST 18%) or a flat amount (a 300 rupee service
  charge). Each tax is spread either by share, in proportion to what each
  person consumed, or equally for flat per-head charges.
- **Bill round-off.** Shops round the printed total, so 103.33 becomes 103 or
  104. Choose nearest whole unit (the GST rule, where 50 paise and over rounds
  up), always round up, or type the exact printed figure. The difference is
  spread across the same split so the shares still add up to the printed
  total.
- **Who paid.** One person or several, splitting what they put in equally, by
  exact amounts, or by percentage.
- **How it splits.** Equally, by exact amounts, by percentage, or by shares
  (1x, 2x and so on), and anyone not involved can be deselected.
- **Settle up.** Two views of the same balances. Actual debts means everyone
  pays back whoever covered them, with debts inside a pair and circular debt
  cancelled. Simplified debts re-routes the same balances into the fewest
  possible payments. Both leave every person in the same position, and
  settling in one view updates the other. Settlements can be partial and can
  be undone.
- **Sharing.** Any group summary or single debt can go out as WhatsApp ready
  text, a PNG card, or a detailed PDF statement listing every expense, its
  taxes, who paid and what each person owes.
- **Insights.** Daily spend charts per group and across all groups, plus a
  breakdown of which group the money goes to.
- **Moving data.** Export a whole profile or a single group as JSON and import
  it anywhere. Groups carry stable random ids, so re-importing merges rather
  than duplicating, and conflicts or possible duplicates are shown for review
  before anything is written.

## How the money maths works

Every amount is stored as an integer number of minor units (paise, cents) and
split with largest-remainder allocation, so shares always add back up to the
total exactly. A bill that does not divide evenly leaves one unit over, so the
app keeps a rounding ledger per group and hands each leftover to whoever is
furthest behind. Totals come out even whenever the arithmetic allows it, and
nobody is ever more than one minor unit from their exact share.

## How it compares

It covers the same ground as Splitwise for splitting group expenses and
settling up, including simplify debts, but runs entirely on device with no
account, no item limits and no adverts. It does not handle payments, currency
conversion, or syncing between people's phones; you share a receipt instead.
One currency per group, chosen when the group is created.

## Technical notes

A plain ES module progressive web app: no framework, no build step, no runtime
dependencies beyond a vendored copy of Apache ECharts for the charts. Data
lives in IndexedDB, falling back to localStorage. A service worker precaches
the app so it launches with no network. Content Security Policy is strict and
the app makes no outbound requests of any kind.
